factor.name: Protocol age (days)
factor.scoring_methodology:
**What this measures**
This factor records the number of days between today and the earliest mainnet deployment of any contract currently live under this protocol. Age is measured from on-chain data rather than team announcements and is updated continuously. It serves as the primary eligibility floor for an A grade under rubric v1.5, which requires a protocol to have been live for at least twelve months.

**Why it matters**
Protocol age is the best single proxy for cumulative battle-testing. Young protocols have had less time to attract white-hat scrutiny, accumulate community monitoring coverage, or demonstrate upgrade discipline under production conditions. The dataset shows a pronounced clustering of exploits in protocols fewer than ninety days old: Eminence Finance was drained on the same day speculative deposits arrived; MobiusDAO was exploited at three days old; Kokomo Finance at under a week. Even for protocols with audits, the early-life period represents the highest-risk window because real production stress has not yet surfaced edge cases.

**Green / Yellow / Red**
Green: protocol is live on mainnet for more than twelve months with no major contract redeployment that resets the clock. Yellow: protocol is between six and twelve months old, or is over twelve months old but redeployed core contracts in the trailing year, effectively resetting the battle-testing clock. Red: protocol is fewer than six months old, or any core contract holding user funds was deployed or redeployed within the last ninety days without a re-audit.

**Common gray cases**
Protocols that launched on a testnet well before mainnet often claim longer effective age; this factor is scored from mainnet deployment only, not testnet dates, so curator verification of the on-chain deploy block is required.

**Notable historical examples**
- **Eminence Finance** ($15M, 2020): Drained within hours of speculative deposits arriving to contracts that had never been publicly announced.
- **Grim Finance** ($30M, 2021): Very new protocol at time of exploit; no established monitoring or white-hat community coverage.
- **StableMagnet** ($27M, 2021): Exploited weeks after launch before any meaningful audit or review cycle.

Phase-1 BTC staking layer live since 2024-08-22 (~621 days to assessment date). Genesis chain live since 2025-04-10 (~389 days). Primary TVL-bearing surface (Phase-1 Bitcoin UTXOs) clears 365-day threshold. Both layers exceed the minimum green threshold.

Protocol age: ~2,280 days since Tinlake v0.2.x first deployment audited April 2020. Even by narrowest definition (V3 Root deployed Aug 1 2024), age is >365 days at profile date. Well above 365-day threshold on all definitions.
Business Wire announced deBridge's mainnet launch on 2022-02-17. That public launch date is more than 365 days before this assessment, meeting the green age threshold.
EigenLayer's Stage 1 mainnet launch was announced on 14 June 2023 with Ethereum mainnet contract addresses. It has therefore operated for more than two years at this refresh date.
Public reporting records USDe and sUSDe launching on 2024-02-19. At the 2026-07-24 refresh date, Ethena has operated for more than 29 months, exceeding the v1.7 green age threshold.

The Ether.fi Nodes Manager was created on Ethereum in 2023; it remains active on the public explorer. At the 2026-07-24 assessment date, this operating history is well above the 365-day green threshold.

The public Arbiscan record for the active Bridge2 contract establishes a June 2023 mainnet deployment. As of 2026-07-24, the protocol has been live for more than 1,100 days, exceeding the 12-month threshold.
JitoSOL's public stake-pool record identifies a 2022-10-31 launch. At the 2026-07-24 assessment date the active Solana surface is well beyond the 365-day green threshold.
